To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electrospinning of 2-methyl 4-nitro-aniline (MNA), which is a highly polar molecule, with a polymer, poly(l-lactic-acid) (PLLA), results in the production of nanofibers that are capable of second harmonic generation (SHG) as strong as pure crystals of MNA in powder form.

we have demonstrated that the electrospun fibers of MNA are highly efficient second-order nonlinear optical devices, and that the efficiency of the fibers is comparable with the efficiency of pure crystalline MNA.
the electrospun polymer nanofibrous materials with guest molecules possessing polar and/or nonlinear optical properties can be an effective method to produce all-organic molecular devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new organic nonlinear optical (NLO) materials, and in particular the synthesis and characterization of a new series of NLO materials based on a 2-(2′-methyl-4-n-pentylphenylimino)-5-(2″-methyl-5″-nitrophenyl)-1,3,4-oxadiazole (MNPPOD) chromophore.
the synthesis, characterization, and application of organic nonlinear optical materials.
the development of new organic molecular materials with high second-order nonlinear optical properties for applications in nonlinear optics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrospun fibers are a new class of molecularly oriented materials that are capable of exhibiting strong nonlinear optical properties.
this study provides an effective way to produce all-organic molecular devices based on electrospun fibers with nonlinear optical and/or other polar molecules as guest species.

this study provides a clear example that the electrospun polymer nanofibrous materials with guest molecules can be an effective method to produce functional materials for molecular electronic and photonic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrospun polymer fibers are capable of producing a single-crystal-like oriented molecular arrangement, which is a key factor for the enhancement of optical nonlinearity.
the molecular arrangement in the nanofibers can be controlled by the electrospun conditions, and the molecular arrangement can be used to control the nonlinear optical properties.

the electrospun nanomaterials are promising for applications of optical devices and nonlinear optical materials, and the technique is also a promising method to fabricate organic functional nanomaterials with molecular orientation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electrospinning can be used to produce highly aligned arrays of nanofibers that can be used to fabricate molecular functional devices based solely on organic materials.
electrospinning can be an effective method to create all-organic molecular devices based on polymer fibers with guest molecules possessing nonlinear optical properties.
the electrospun fibers can be used to produce highly efficient optical devices based on the nonlinear properties of guest molecules.
